shared_elements: low-relief carved surface on a vertical shaft
glyph-like blocks arranged in vertical columns
possible standing figure or figural relief on the shaft
justification: Both are upright rectangular relief-carved shafts whose faces carry rectilinear sign-blocks arranged in paired vertical columns running the full height, a fairly specific and conventional scheme. The main difference is that A's visible face appears dominated by a figural relief with only subsidiary text panels, while B shows a purely glyphic surface with no discernible figure, and A's carving is far more worn so its forms are only partly legible.
